stances.summary: Warns against neglecting public health infrastructure and preparedness
stances.quote:
3 years ago I wrote this piece for @theatlantic.com about why we mustn’t take public health for granted.

This is long before this admin’s deep cuts to public health.

With the massive Cyclospora outbreak, I couldn’t help thinking about my own warning from the past.

stances.summary: Criticizes U.S. abandoning hard-won Ebola response lessons
stances.quote:
For @theatlantic.com, I wrote about all the lessons we've learned over the last decade in battling Ebola

And how the U.S. appears hellbent on learning them all over again, the hard way.

Gift link below:
www.theatlantic.com/health/2026/...

stances.summary: Criticizes current U.S. Ebola response as breaking with established global health policy
stances.quote:
New in @thelancet.com with @krutikakuppalli.bsky.social, Martin Cetron, and @drdebhoury.bsky.social — we argue the current US response to the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo and Uganda is breaking with longstanding global health policy in very worrying ways.

www.thelancet.com/journal

stances.summary: Expresses concerns about Ebola outbreak response and community resistance
stances.quote:
A month into the growing Ebola outbreak, I wrote about what worries me, why the numbers don’t tell the whole story, and why communities are understandably pushing back on the response.

open.substack.com/pub/craigasp...

stances.summary: Questions whether AI will erode physicians' clinical writing skills
stances.quote:
A brilliant essay by my friend @helenouyang.bsky.social in the New York Times Magazine.

Writing notes is one of my least favorite parts of working in the ER. But learning how to write them teaches physicians important skills.

What impact will AI have on that skill?

www.nytimes

stances.summary: Assesses Ebola outbreak response, notes progress and ongoing concerns
stances.quote:
Three weeks into the growing Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo and Uganda, I take stock of what’s working well, and what still worries me.

All that and more, and all for free, on my Substack 👇

stances.summary: Warns U.S. is abandoning proven Ebola control strategies
stances.quote: Craig Spencer has followed every Ebola outbreak since 2014 and seen how the world’s capacity to control the virus has improved—but the U.S. is forgetting what made that possible, he argues.

stances.summary: Highlights healthcare worker burden during disease outbreak response
stances.quote: Professor @craigspencer.bsky.social shared his personal Ebola story with @markpatinkin.bsky.social. “I had been taking care of 30 to 40 patients at any one point in Guinea,” he said, “and now there were 30 to 40 people to take care of me.”
